newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ may change rate policy in late 97--Yamaichi.
newsitem.headline: BOJ may change rate policy in late 97--Yamaichi.

text.p: The Bank of Japan is likely to change its low interest rate policy in the autumn of 1997 when the economic trend for the July-September period is known, Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc, a private research body, said on Thursday.

"The monetary authorities will likely correct their current super-low interest rate policy when it is clear that an increase in the consumption tax in April had only a temporary effect on the economy," Yamaichi said in a report.
The consumption tax is due to be raised to five percent from three percent on April 1.
Yamaichi said Japan's gross domestic product (GDP) is likely to grow 1.7 percent in real terms in the fiscal year starting on April 1, compared with estimated growth of 2.7 percent in 1996/97.

Yamaichi said it expects Japan's GDP to show a quarter-on-quarter fall of 1.0 percent in the April-June period, due mainly to the negative impact of the tax hike, but added that it may bounce back and grow at a level of slightly less than one percent in the July-September period.
Yamaichi said call rates were most likely to be raised in late 1997, but added it was possible rates would be increased by about 0.25 point in the current fiscal year to March 31.
On average, call rates have been kept at below the official discount rate since September last year when the BOJ cut the discount rate to a historic low of 0.5 percent.
